headline: High: shared MCP/file pathways can leak sensitive context into a writable Replit workspace, and default Replit shell/git/network powers make cascading mistakes plausible.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: MemMachine exposes an MCP server and REST/Python interfaces, while Replit Agent can read/write the Repl filesystem and run shell commands. If MemMachine outputs are bridged into the Repl workspace or MCP channel, Replit Agent may treat attacker-controlled content as instructions. The pairwise pathway is plausible but not directly documented.
conditions: IF MemMachine outputs are copied into a Replit file or prompt that Replit Agent reads as trusted text
IF a shared MCP or file bridge is configured between the two agents
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of MemMachine outputs into Replit prompts
Require explicit human review before Replit Agent acts on any MemMachine-generated text
Store MemMachine outputs in a non-executable, read-only location
Add a prompt-injection filter to any bridge between the agents
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging on all cross-agent content

B_data_leakage.rationale: MemMachine touches long-term user facts and conversational context, and Replit Agent touches source code, secrets, and deployment configuration. Replit Agent also has broad network egress and secret handling, so if MemMachine context is placed into the Repl workspace or prompt, sensitive data can flow into a third-party service. The interaction is inferred from documented surfaces, not directly observed.
conditions: IF MemMachine context or user facts are copied into the Repl workspace or prompt
IF Replit Agent is allowed to transmit workspace contents to external services during normal operation
mitigations: Keep MemMachine data out of the Repl workspace unless redacted
Separate secrets from any shared prompt or file bridge
Turn off or restrict outbound network access for the Repl during cross-agent review
Use a minimal, sanitized handoff file between agents
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention checks on cross-agent transfers

C_capability_conflict.rationale: MemMachine can use MCP and API surfaces, while Replit Agent can execute shell commands, modify git state, and write the filesystem in a persistent Repl workspace. If both are pointed at the same mutable repo or workspace, they can overwrite each other's changes without coordination. The profiles document overlapping write authority, so the conflict pathway is credible.
conditions: IF both agents are connected to the same repository or workspace
IF either agent is allowed to write files or commit changes without locking
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate workspace
Pause one agent before the other writes to the repo
Use git branches with manual merge review
Disable automatic commit or push actions
requires-engineering: add file-locking or lease-based coordination

D_cascading_error.rationale: MemMachine can generate context-rich outputs, and Replit Agent can act on them with shell, package, and git tools. If Replit Agent treats MemMachine output as authoritative, mistakes can cascade into code changes or deployment actions. Replit checkpoints reduce but do not eliminate the risk, so medium fits better than low.
conditions: IF Replit Agent is instructed to implement or deploy MemMachine-produced recommendations without verification
IF MemMachine output is used as the sole source for code or configuration changes
mitigations: Require a second review before any shell or git action
Ask Replit Agent to cite the exact source line before acting
Compare MemMachine output against an independent check
Limit Replit Agent to draft-only changes
requires-engineering: add automated validation gates before deployment

E_compliance.rationale: MemMachine touches long-term user facts and conversational context, while Replit Agent handles source code, secrets, and deployment configuration in a cloud Repl. That creates a plausible retention and residency mismatch if the same personal data is moved into Replit's environment. The profiles do not prove a specific legal violation, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF personal data from MemMachine is transferred into the Replit workspace
IF the deployment must satisfy stricter retention or residency rules than the Repl environment provides
mitigations: Avoid moving regulated personal data into Replit
Redact identifiers before handoff
Document retention and deletion steps for both systems
Keep secrets in the designated secrets store only
requires-engineering: perform a formal residency and retention review
